payload.claim: `check_readiness` wraps every other step's failure in a try/except and converts it to a named `Readiness(False, step, detail)`, but the disk-headroom step calls `disk_headroom_ok(home)` unguarded. `disk_headroom_ok` is documented and tested to *raise* `RuntimeError` rather than read a check-that-could-not-run as a pass (line ~318-333), and that raise is never caught here, so it propagates straight out of `check_readiness` as a bare exception. This directly contradicts the contract stated on `Readiness` itself two lines above (line ~373): 'never a bare boolean, so a caller can skip the repo and say why ... instead of discovering the reason by reading a traceback the first cell raised' — for exactly the disk-full/unreadable case that promise exists to cover, the caller gets the traceback anyway.
